Quentin Coleman.off: Combo guard who shoots off the ball and now runs the offense.
Quentin Coleman.def: Active guard who rebounds and gets steals.
Quentin Coleman.str: He shoots it (50.6% from three as a senior), finishes above the rim, and crashes the glass. He led Team USA U18 in rebounding and is averaging 4.7 assists as Illinois' lead guard.
Quentin Coleman.weak: He's 6'4" and slim, and he has to prove the high-volume three holds against Big Ten length.
Quentin Coleman.swing: Running an offense full time. If the playmaking sticks, he's a top-5 pick.
Quentin Coleman.why_comp: Mitchell is the explosive 6'3" guard who rebounds, gets steals and started off the ball before taking over as a creator. Suggs is the athletic two-way guard who plays passing lanes and scores without being a full-time point guard. Grimes is the floor: an athletic 6'4" guard who shoots and defends but never became a creator.
Quentin Coleman.outlets: ESPN 6, B/R 8, NDR 3, FanSided 8, HoopObsession 6, Tankathon 22. Consensus 8.8. CBS: Coleman has no off switch.
Quentin Coleman.why: A shooter, rebounder and athlete who is already running a top-10 team's offense at 18.

Andrej Stojakovic.off: Slashing wing who creates his own shot and lives in the midrange.
Andrej Stojakovic.str: He scores at all three levels and gets to the line. He had a career-high 46 on 14-21 shooting and 16-20 at the line at No. 5.
Andrej Stojakovic.weak: He's 22.9 on draft night, on his third school, and he's 8-24 from three.
Andrej Stojakovic.swing: The three. Efficient volume as a lead option decides whether he's a first-rounder.
Andrej Stojakovic.why_comp: LeVert is the 6'7" slasher who creates his own shot and made it as an older prospect. Jaquez is the crafty older slasher who scores from midrange and draws fouls (Illinois on SI's comparison). Johnson is the floor: a downhill wing whose jumper never came, so his role shrank.
Andrej Stojakovic.outlets: ESPN 59, B/R 60, Tankathon 37. Consensus 52.0, so I'm much higher than the field.
Andrej Stojakovic.why: He's carrying a top-10 team as a scorer. His age and shooting keep him out of the lottery.

Ethan Brown.str: He's shooting 51.3% from three (20-39) with 4.6 assists and 5.7 rebounds, and he won a starting job on a top-10 team as a three-star freshman.
Ethan Brown.weak: Small sample against soft competition. 26 of his early points came in a blowout of Eastern Illinois.
Ethan Brown.swing: Keeping it up against Big Ten defenses and real length.
Ethan Brown.why_comp: White came out of a small school, stands 6'4" and wins by shooting, passing and rebounding without turning it over. Huerter is a right-handed shooter who isn't built big and can make the extra pass. Gillespie is the floor: a smart shooting guard who went undrafted and stuck.
Ethan Brown.outlets: Not on any outlet board yet. Illinois on SI and The Ticket have covered his start.
Ethan Brown.why: His production is real so far. The competition and sample keep him in the 20s.

Tomislav Ivisic.off: Pick-and-pop center who shoots on volume and passes.
Tomislav Ivisic.def: Drop big who struggles in space.
Tomislav Ivisic.str: He's a skilled 7'1" shooter and passer, hitting 34% from three on real volume.
Tomislav Ivisic.weak: He'll be 23.9 on draft night, he's heavy-footed on defense, and 4.4 rebounds is low for his size.
Tomislav Ivisic.swing: Defending in space. If he can't guard pick-and-rolls, he's a two-way contract at best.
Tomislav Ivisic.why_comp: Olynyk is the skilled 7-foot shooter and passer who lasted a decade. Landale is the backup big who shoots and passes. Petrusev is the floor: a skilled European big who gets a look.
Tomislav Ivisic.outlets: Tankathon No. 56. NBA Draft Room projects mid first to mid second round. Yahoo called him a second-round pick at best.
Tomislav Ivisic.why: The skill is real. The age and defense put him at the bottom of the board.

Tyran Stokes.off: Forward who brings it up and makes plays.
Tyran Stokes.str: He gets to the paint on his own at 230 pounds, sees the floor on the move, and rebounds.
Tyran Stokes.weak: 67.5% at the line, 2.6 turnovers to 2.0 assists, and efficiency in big games (he lost to Houston despite 22 and 11).
Tyran Stokes.swing: Decision-making. The shot has shown up so far.
Tyran Stokes.why_comp: Johnson is the strong, athletic point forward who became an All-Star-level creator. Gordon is the powerful forward who wins with strength, passing and defense. Tate is the floor: a strong forward who sticks as a passer and rebounder if the shot fades. ESPN's high school comp was Scottie Barnes, and NBADraft.net uses Caron Butler.
Tyran Stokes.why: Biggest combination of size, strength and playmaking in the class, and every outlet agrees.

Bruce Branch III.def: Wing stopper because of his length.
Bruce Branch III.str: A 7'1" wingspan, he blocks shots from the wing, and he's very young for the class.
Bruce Branch III.weak: 51.4% at the line is a red flag for a shooter. Thin frame, and he floats through stretches.
Bruce Branch III.swing: Free throws and catch-and-shoot threes. A 51% free-throw shooter rarely turns into a 38% NBA three-point shooter.
Bruce Branch III.why_comp: Murphy is the long shooting wing who became a big-time starter. Vassell is a long, thin shooting wing who blocks shots and makes plays on defense, which is what Branch does at 6'7" and 190. Reddish is the floor: all the length, never consistent.
Bruce Branch III.outlets: ESPN 3, B/R 4, CBS 4, NDR 5, FanSided 11, HoopObsession 9, Tankathon 4. Consensus 5.7.
Bruce Branch III.why: The tools are top-3 level, but the free-throw shooting could push him down if it lasts.

Caleb Holt.def: Guards the other team's best guard.
Caleb Holt.str: Physical defender, 2.6 steals, rebounds like a forward, and 91% at the line.
Caleb Holt.weak: 1.2 assists is low for a combo guard, and the three is streaky.
Caleb Holt.swing: The jumper. The free throws say it can come.
Caleb Holt.why_comp: Holiday is the strong two-way guard who defends and scores (NBADraft.net uses Jrue Holiday / Caris LeVert). Hart is the rebounding guard who does everything (ESPN's comp). Brown is the floor: the strong, physical guard who rebounds and defends if the jumper never fully comes.
Caleb Holt.outlets: ESPN 5, B/R 3, CBS 3, NDR 11, FanSided 4, HoopObsession 2, Tankathon 2. Consensus 4.3.
Caleb Holt.why: Highest floor of the freshmen. The defense and rebounding translate on day one.

Ivan Kharchenkov.off: Wing who attacks closeouts and makes plays from the second side.
Ivan Kharchenkov.def: Guards the other team's best scorer.
Ivan Kharchenkov.str: A known defender who now scores (38 vs UCLA), passes and rebounds.
Ivan Kharchenkov.weak: Low three-point volume, 3.0 turnovers a game, and he shot 31.7% from three last season.
Ivan Kharchenkov.swing: Three-point volume. If he stays at 40% on 5+ attempts, he's a lottery pick.
Ivan Kharchenkov.why_comp: Avdija is the European wing who passes, rebounds, defends and grew into a scorer. Batum is the version where the passing and defense carry a long career. Larsson is the floor: a GoPHNX writer called him the prototype for Ivan, the Swiss Army knife Tommy Lloyd loves.
Ivan Kharchenkov.outlets: ESPN 11, B/R 14, CBS 25, NDR 8, FanSided 10, HoopObsession 28, Tankathon 18. Consensus 16.3.
Ivan Kharchenkov.why: Most productive player on a top-10 team, and his defense was proven before the scoring arrived.

Braylon Mullins.str: 10 threes a game at 38%, moves well off the ball, and he had 29 against Arizona.
Braylon Mullins.weak: 41.4 FG% means he isn't finishing inside. 3 rebounds and 1.6 assists.
Braylon Mullins.swing: Whether he can score inside the arc. Shooters who can't finish get capped.
Braylon Mullins.why_comp: Green is the 3-and-D ceiling. Trent is a scoring guard with solid positional size and athleticism (Last Word on Sports' comp). Merrill is the floor: a shooter who earned a real role.
Braylon Mullins.outlets: ESPN 8, B/R 12, CBS 8, NDR 17, FanSided 33, HoopObsession 17, Tankathon 10. Consensus 15.0.
Braylon Mullins.why: Elite shooting on volume always gets drafted early, and he's doing it against good teams.

Jason Crowe Jr..off: Lead scorer who creates off the dribble.
Jason Crowe Jr..str: Creates his own shot, 39.5% from three on volume, 91% at the line, and one of the youngest players in the class.
Jason Crowe Jr..weak: 3.0 turnovers to 3.7 assists, 2.7 rebounds, and guarding bigger guards.
Jason Crowe Jr..swing: Passing. If he becomes a real point guard, he's top 5.
Jason Crowe Jr..why_comp: Simons is the young shot-maker who became a 20-point scorer. Monk is the microwave bench scorer. Hardy is the floor: a young scorer who never got efficient.
Jason Crowe Jr..outlets: ESPN 21, B/R 23, CBS 17, FanSided 28, HoopObsession 8, Tankathon 16. Consensus 18.8.
Jason Crowe Jr..why: An 18-year-old who already shoots like this is rare. The passing is the bet.

Amari Allen.off: Wing who runs some offense and makes the right read.
Amari Allen.str: 6 assists to 0.6 turnovers, 50% from three, and a triple-double vs Arkansas State. He also posted a 42.5-inch max vertical at the 2026 combine.
Amari Allen.weak: He needs to create against length.
Amari Allen.swing: Creating his own shot. Today he wins with reads.
Amari Allen.why_comp: Middleton is the big wing who grew into a shot creator. George is a versatile wing who can contribute in various ways (Last Word on Sports' comp). O'Neale is the floor: a high-IQ wing who shoots and connects.
Amari Allen.outlets: ESPN 19, B/R 13, CBS 9, NDR 9, FanSided 24, HoopObsession 13, Tankathon 12. Consensus 14.1.
Amari Allen.why: Best decision-maker among the wings, and his shooting is real.

Alijah Arenas.str: Size and handle for a shooting guard, he gets to the line, and he's been efficient so far.
Alijah Arenas.weak: 2.2 assists, shot selection last year, and injury history (car accident, torn meniscus).
Alijah Arenas.swing: Whether the efficiency holds once Big Ten play starts.
Alijah Arenas.why_comp: Beal is the big shooting guard who became a primary scorer. Thomas is the bucket-getter off the bench. Beasley is the floor: a shooter-scorer who sticks.
Alijah Arenas.outlets: ESPN 20, B/R 10, CBS 14, NDR 7, FanSided 58, Tankathon 29. Consensus 23.0.
Alijah Arenas.why: Tools plus production. The outlets range from 7 to 58, so I'm betting on the version we're seeing now.

Stefan Joksimovic.str: 6'7" with point guard vision, playing EuroLeague minutes at 18, and U18 EuroBasket MVP (23.1 PPG).
Stefan Joksimovic.weak: 26.7% from three, 63.9% at the line, and 4.9 points in EuroLeague.
Stefan Joksimovic.swing: Shooting. Right now his free throws and threes are both below average.
Stefan Joksimovic.why_comp: Giddey is a big lefty creator with a shaky jumper, which fits as a realistic ceiling. Maledon is the French guard who carved out a role. Hayes is the lefty floor: a big European point guard who never shot it.
Stefan Joksimovic.outlets: ESPN 2, B/R 6, CBS 5, NDR 2, FanSided 2, HoopObsession 5, Tankathon 5. Consensus 3.9.
Stefan Joksimovic.why: This is my biggest gap below the outlets. The talent is top 5, but I want production before I move him up.

Obinna Ekezie Jr..str: 7'2" and blocks shots, makes threes, and had 20 and 13 against Morehead State.
Obinna Ekezie Jr..weak: Only 16 minutes behind Bidunga, 0.2 assists, and shoulder surgery earlier in 2026.
Obinna Ekezie Jr..swing: Minutes. He needs 25 a night to prove he can carry this production.
Obinna Ekezie Jr..why_comp: Turner is the 7-foot shot blocker who spaces the floor. Bamba is the long stretch big in a backup role. Jones is the floor: a long, bouncy big who hangs on.
Obinna Ekezie Jr..why: A 7'2" rim protector who shoots is rare. The minutes keep him out of the top 10.

Jordan Smith Jr..def: Guards the other team's best guard.
Jordan Smith Jr..str: Strength and burst at his size, a long wingspan and 2.0 steals a game.
Jordan Smith Jr..weak: About 53 TS%, only 5 threes attempted, and 2.4 assists to 2.2 turnovers.
Jordan Smith Jr..swing: The jumper. He made 37% of his threes as a high school senior, so it's in there.
Jordan Smith Jr..why_comp: Bledsoe is the strong, explosive guard who defended and drove his way to a long career (also NBADraft.net's comparison). Mitchell is the tough point-of-attack defender in a rotation. Dennis Smith Jr. is the floor: an explosive guard whose shot never came, who stuck as a defender.
Jordan Smith Jr..outlets: ESPN 4, B/R 2, CBS 2, NDR 4, FanSided 3, HoopObsession 3, Tankathon 3. Consensus 3.0.
Jordan Smith Jr..why: The outlets have him at 3, so this is my biggest fade. A 6'2" guard has to score efficiently to stay up top, and he hasn't yet.

Motiejus Krivas.str: Size, soft hands, 81% at the line, and he anchors an elite defense.
Motiejus Krivas.swing: Whether he can survive switches. In the NBA, guards will target him.
Motiejus Krivas.why_comp: Valanciunas is the strong Lithuanian post center who started for a decade. Nurkic is the big-bodied passer and rebounder. Baynes is the floor: a physical backup who sets screens and defends the rim.
Motiejus Krivas.outlets: ESPN 7, B/R 19, CBS 16, NDR 12, FanSided 9, HoopObsession 19, Tankathon 23. Consensus 15.0.
Motiejus Krivas.why: His production is top 10, but a senior big who can't switch has a ceiling.

Thomas Haugh.str: Athletic and tough, shooting it great so far, and he rarely turns it over.
Thomas Haugh.weak: He's 24 on draft night, shot 32.6% from three last year, and isn't a creator.
Thomas Haugh.swing: Whether the three is real this time.
Thomas Haugh.why_comp: Parsons is the 6'9" shooting forward who started (NBADraft.net uses Chandler Parsons / Jaime Jaquez Jr.). Green is the versatile forward who lasts on toughness and size (B/R's realistic comparison). Wade is the floor: a long forward who spaces and defends in a role.
Thomas Haugh.outlets: ESPN 9, B/R 21, CBS 6, NDR 10, FanSided 41, HoopObsession 22, Tankathon 14. Consensus 17.6.
Thomas Haugh.why: He's ready to play now, but the senior cap keeps him behind the younger upside guys.

Patrick Ngongba II.off: Hub at the elbow and in the post.
Patrick Ngongba II.weak: Injury history, foul trouble, and he looked overmatched against Illinois.
Patrick Ngongba II.swing: Staying healthy and holding up against real size.
Patrick Ngongba II.why_comp: Hartenstein is the passing center who became a starter on a contender. Bitadze is the skilled backup big. Bassey is the floor: a shot-blocking backup who sticks. Sportscasting goes much higher with Marc Gasol and Al Jefferson.
Patrick Ngongba II.outlets: ESPN 10, B/R 7, CBS 10, NDR 29, FanSided 6, HoopObsession 16, Tankathon 15. Consensus 13.3.
Patrick Ngongba II.why: The numbers say lottery, the eye test says late first. 15 splits the difference.

Malachi Moreno.off: Roll man and passer from the short roll.
Malachi Moreno.str: He runs the floor, has good hands, and averages 3 assists a game for a center.
Malachi Moreno.weak: A 25.5-inch no-step vertical and 29.0 max at the combine, plus 62.5% at the line and no jumper.
Malachi Moreno.swing: Strength. He has to hold position against NBA centers.
Malachi Moreno.why_comp: Allen is the mobile, sure-handed center who started for years. Collins is the skilled backup big who passes. Brown is the floor: a big who sticks on size and rebounding (NBADraft.net's comparison).
Malachi Moreno.outlets: ESPN 14, B/R 34, CBS 18, FanSided 19, HoopObsession 29, Tankathon 30. Consensus 24.0.
Malachi Moreno.why: Young, efficient, and he passes. Bigs like that keep getting drafted in the teens.

Luigi Suigo.off: Screener, roll man and occasional shooter.
Luigi Suigo.str: Massive size, rebounding, and he made 18 threes as a pro last year.
Luigi Suigo.weak: Mobility in space, 3-7 at the line, and only 5 college games so far.
Luigi Suigo.swing: The three. A 7'3" shooter goes in the lottery.
Luigi Suigo.why_comp: Lopez is the giant who became a stretch five and anchored a title defense. Kalkbrenner is the big drop center in a role (B/R's Wasserman made this comparison). Marjanovic is the floor: a giant who sticks as a third center.
Luigi Suigo.outlets: ESPN 29, B/R 32, CBS 7, NDR 14, FanSided 40, HoopObsession 21, Tankathon 21. Consensus 23.4.
Luigi Suigo.why: I have him here because of his size and the shooting potential.

Hugo Yimga-Moukouri.str: Athleticism and strength, scoring against adults at 18, and 40.5% from three in Betclic ELITE last year.
Hugo Yimga-Moukouri.weak: 0.6 assists, shooting down to 31% this season, limited creating.
Hugo Yimga-Moukouri.swing: The three. With it, he's a 3-and-D forward. Without it, he's a bench defender.
Hugo Yimga-Moukouri.why_comp: Anunoby is the strong, athletic forward who defends anyone and shoots enough to start. Coulibaly is the long French wing defender. Cissoko is the floor: a strong French wing who sticks on defense.
Hugo Yimga-Moukouri.outlets: ESPN 28, B/R 27, NDR 20, FanSided 30, HoopObsession 7, Tankathon 11. Consensus 20.5. Floor and Ceiling's read is defense-first.
Hugo Yimga-Moukouri.why: I'm betting on an athlete producing against pros at 18.

Tounde Yessoufou.str: Strength, rebounding, and 44% from three after shooting 29.3% last year.
Tounde Yessoufou.swing: Whether the jump to 44% from three holds over a full season.
Tounde Yessoufou.why_comp: Oladipo is the strong, explosive two-way guard at his peak. Dort is the physical wing stopper who shoots enough (NBADraft.net's comparison). Diallo is the floor: an explosive wing who sticks on athleticism.
Tounde Yessoufou.outlets: ESPN 44, B/R 31, CBS 13, FanSided 57, HoopObsession 37, Tankathon 19. Consensus 33.5.
Tounde Yessoufou.why: He moved up on strength and his shooting jump. Outlets are still split from 13 to 57.

Tyler Tanner.weak: 5'10" barefoot, and 4-20 from three after 36.8% last year.
Tyler Tanner.swing: The three. Small guards have to shoot.
Tyler Tanner.why_comp: VanVleet is the undersized guard who shot and defended his way to a title (Sports Business Classroom's comparison). Lawson is the blur-quick point guard who ran a good offense. Chandler is the floor: a small, quick backup.
Tyler Tanner.outlets: ESPN 30, CBS 19, FanSided 5, HoopObsession 12, Tankathon 32. Consensus 19.6.
Tyler Tanner.why: All-American production, but size and the cold start keep him out of the top 20.

Daniel Jacobsen.str: Size, touch (86.8% at the line), passing and footwork.
Daniel Jacobsen.weak: Injury-shortened freshman year, a small sample of college minutes, and strength.
Daniel Jacobsen.swing: Staying healthy for a full season.
Daniel Jacobsen.why_comp: Clingan is the giant rim protector who starts (Jacobsen has said he plays like a cross between Clingan and Kyle Filipowski). Ware is the long, skilled backup center. Koloko is the floor: a long shot blocker who sticks.
Daniel Jacobsen.why: 19 points on 76 TS% at 7'3" with 87% free throws. The outlets haven't caught up yet.

Colben Landrew.off: Attacks closeouts and drives through contact.
Colben Landrew.def: Switches 2 through 4 and guards bigger wings.
Colben Landrew.str: He has an NBA body already. He finishes through contact and rebounds well for a wing.
Colben Landrew.weak: He's 3-14 from three. His handle is mostly straight-line, and he has little pull-up game.
Colben Landrew.swing: Corner three. If it hits 35%, he's a starter.
Colben Landrew.why_comp: Okoro fits him almost exactly: a strong 6'5" slasher who defended right away and needed years to fix his jumper. Brooks is the version where the shot comes around and he defends with real edge. Champagnie is the floor: a strong-bodied wing who sticks on rebounding and effort.
Colben Landrew.outlets: Consensus has him at 12.6, so I'm about 10 spots lower than the field.
Colben Landrew.why: He's built for the NBA and fits a role, but his shooting doesn't support a lottery pick yet.

Alex Condon.def: Drops and shows on pick-and-rolls, with some switching.
Alex Condon.str: His passing is among the best of any big in the class. He moves his feet well in space.
Alex Condon.weak: He's a senior, 22.9 on draft night. He's light for a center and has no reliable jumper.
Alex Condon.swing: Strength. Can he hold position against NBA centers?
Alex Condon.why_comp: Plumlee was a mobile, high-feel passing big who started for good teams. Poeltl is the version who adds strength and holds up as a full-time starting center. Theis is the floor: a smart, mobile backup who lasted years.
Alex Condon.outlets: Yahoo Sports compared him to Isaiah Hartenstein. Jonathan Givony praised how Condon triggers Florida's offense with his feel for the game.
Alex Condon.why: His feel and passing are bankable. His age caps the upside.

Caleb Gaskins.def: Guards forwards and helps at the rim.
Caleb Gaskins.str: He's long, explosive and strong, at 18.9 on draft night.
Caleb Gaskins.weak: 52.4 TS% is poor. His shot selection and decisions are raw.
Caleb Gaskins.why_comp: Grant is the outcome where he becomes an athletic forward who can score on the second side. Kenrich Williams is the glue-forward version. Bates-Diop is a long forward who stuck around as a backup.
Caleb Gaskins.outlets: NBADraft.net comps him to Joey Graham. ESPN's way-too-early mock projected him at No. 11. Consensus now has him at 22.5.
Caleb Gaskins.why: I'm betting on youth and tools. The efficiency has to show up by February.

Dylan Mingo.off: Secondary ball handler who pushes in transition.
Dylan Mingo.def: Point-of-attack defender who jumps passing lanes.
Dylan Mingo.str: He's 6'5" with a 6'10" wingspan and averages 3.0 steals. He's one of the youngest players on the board.
Dylan Mingo.weak: He's taken almost no threes (0-4), so we don't know about his shot yet.
Dylan Mingo.swing: Whether he takes and makes threes.
Dylan Mingo.why_comp: Murray was a long, steal-heavy point guard who added a jumper and made an All-Star team. Wright is a long two-way backup point guard. Payton is the floor: a big point guard with no shot who still played nine seasons.
Dylan Mingo.outlets: NBADraft.net's comp is Elfrid Payton. Baylor lists him at 6'5" with a 6'10" wingspan.
Dylan Mingo.why: His size and defensive tools are top-20 caliber. His shot is unknown, so he's not higher.

Davis Fogle.str: He's productive in every category. He's a good driver for his frame, and he works the offensive glass.
Davis Fogle.weak: He's thin (he arrived around 185). He's 6-20 from three and only 43.1 from the field.
Davis Fogle.swing: Adding strength so his drives hold up against NBA bodies.
Davis Fogle.why_comp: Hayward was a slender, high-feel 6'8" wing who grew into a creator. Marshall is a driving wing with feel who earns rotation minutes on effort and rebounding. Martin is the floor: a bouncy, rangy forward who stuck as a reserve.
Davis Fogle.outlets: Yardbarker's prospect watch singled out his analytical profile, driving, off-ball defense and offensive rebounding.
Davis Fogle.why: His production and data are first-round level. His frame and shot need time.

Miles Sadler.off: Lead guard scoring off the bounce.
Miles Sadler.str: He's quick and can score at volume as a freshman. He had 18 against No. 1 Florida.
Miles Sadler.weak: He's 6'0" and 170, and 10-42 from three (23.8%) is a real problem for a small guard.
Miles Sadler.swing: Pull-up three. Small guards have to shoot.
Miles Sadler.why_comp: Sexton is the scoring-first small guard whose jumper came around. Schroder is a quick, pesky point guard who carved out a long career. Alvarado is the floor: an undersized guard who sticks on defensive pressure.
Miles Sadler.outlets: West Virginia On SI's Schuyler Callihan wrote that his size will be a real problem for NBA scouts, though he still believes in the production.
Miles Sadler.why: He's one of the best scorers on the board. His size and shooting keep him in the late 20s.

Billy Richmond III.off: Cutter and transition finisher who makes the quick pass.
Billy Richmond III.str: He made the SEC All-Defensive team last year. He's an elite athlete and very efficient this season.
Billy Richmond III.weak: 7-13 from three is a small sample. Shooting has always been his question.
Billy Richmond III.swing: Whether the three-point shooting is real.
Billy Richmond III.why_comp: Jones is the connective stopper who shoots enough to start. Okogie is an athletic wing defender in a rotation role. Green is the floor: a high-energy athlete who sticks on defense.
Billy Richmond III.outlets: Last Word on Sports called three-point shooting the defining obstacle between him and a guaranteed NBA roster spot.
Billy Richmond III.why: His defense alone gets him drafted. If the shooting is real, he moves up.

Anthony Thompson.off: Big shooter off movement and a mismatch scorer.
Anthony Thompson.def: Uses his length on wings and forwards.
Anthony Thompson.str: He's a 6'9" shooter with a 7'3" wingspan, still 18.9 on draft night.
Anthony Thompson.weak: 48.1 TS% is a slow start, and he's light on production.
Anthony Thompson.swing: Getting to 40%+ from the field and earning touches.
Anthony Thompson.why_comp: Porter is the ceiling for a tall shooter who can score on his own. Johnson is the likely version: a big floor-spacer and starter-level shooter. LaRavia is the floor: a skilled forward who sticks as a shooter.
Anthony Thompson.outlets: NBADraft.net comps him to Donyell Marshall. Consensus has him at 15.4.
Anthony Thompson.why: His tools are lottery level. His production isn't yet.

Najai Hines.str: His touch and strength around the rim give him a 75.4 TS%.
Najai Hines.weak: He's heavy, and his conditioning and engagement have been questioned.
Najai Hines.swing: Staying on the floor. That's both conditioning and fouls.
Najai Hines.why_comp: Zubac is the big-bodied drop center who became a reliable starter. Adams is the strong rebounder who sets screens. Sharpe is the floor: a physical backup who rebounds.
Najai Hines.outlets: Jon Rothstein reported Hines is 10 pounds lighter since last season. Roundtable called him the most impactful player in UConn's exhibition opener.
Najai Hines.why: His efficiency and size are real. Teams will want proof of his conditioning.

Abdou Toure.str: He's an elite athlete and was rising late in his recruitment.
Abdou Toure.weak: His role is small so far, and his shot is unproven.
Abdou Toure.swing: His handle. Can he create, not just finish?
Abdou Toure.why_comp: Oubre is the athletic slashing wing who scores in volume. Jones is a high-flying defender in a role. Williams is the floor: a long, athletic wing who stays on a roster.
Abdou Toure.outlets: He said he studies Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Anthony Edwards. Rivals' Jamie Shaw said the upside is incredibly high.
Abdou Toure.why: He has upside, but his production is too thin for a first-round grade right now.

Miikka Muurinen.def: Switches in space and helps at the rim.
Miikka Muurinen.str: He's a 7-footer who can play away from the basket and finish above the rim. He has EuroBasket experience against grown men.
Miikka Muurinen.weak: The efficiency isn't there yet: 3-18 from three and 47.3 TS%. He's thin.
Miikka Muurinen.swing: The three. His whole profile depends on it.
Miikka Muurinen.why_comp: Jabari Smith is the 7-foot shooting four who can defend in space. Jalen Smith is the athletic stretch big who became a useful rotation player. Dieng is the floor: a lanky, skilled forward who stayed on rosters while developing.
Miikka Muurinen.outlets: He won the inaugural EuroBasket 2025 Rising Star award. Consensus has him at 18.7.
Miikka Muurinen.why: His archetype is coveted. His college production so far isn't.

Sayon Keita.str: His length and bounce are rare. He already blocks 2.2 shots in 20.8 minutes.
Sayon Keita.weak: At 215 he's very light. He's only played since 2020, so he's raw.
Sayon Keita.swing: Adding 20 pounds without losing his bounce.
Sayon Keita.why_comp: Lively was a skinny, long rim protector who became a starter on a Finals team. Williams is a lob catcher and shot blocker who starts when healthy. Sims is the floor: a bouncy backup who sticks on rim running.
Sayon Keita.outlets: Coverage of his commitment noted he only started playing basketball in 2020. SI described his UNC role as rebounding, blocking shots, rim running and screening.
Sayon Keita.why: His tools are lottery level. His strength and polish are a year or two away.

JJ Andrews.off: Downhill scorer who posts up smaller wings.
JJ Andrews.str: He has NBA strength already and won EYBL MVP in 2025.
JJ Andrews.weak: He's coming off the bench, and his production is way down. He's not an elite athlete.
JJ Andrews.swing: Getting enough minutes to show what he did over the summer.
JJ Andrews.why_comp: Barnes is the strong, physical wing who became a long-time starter. Crowder is the tough 6'6" combo forward who defends and spaces enough. Martin is the floor: a strong, smart role wing.
JJ Andrews.outlets: NBADraft.net's comp is Marvin Williams. Rivals' Jamie Shaw praised his physicality.
JJ Andrews.why: He fits a role, but his early college numbers don't support where some outlets have him (B/R had him No. 9).

Dame Sarr.def: Guards 1 through 4 and jumps passing lanes.
Dame Sarr.str: He's long and versatile on defense, he's averaging 2.2 steals, and he's been very efficient.
Dame Sarr.weak: He's 4-13 from three and doesn't create much off the dribble.
Dame Sarr.why_comp: McDaniels is the skinny 6'9" defender who guards anyone and hits enough threes to start. Finney-Smith is a 3-and-D forward. Thybulle is the floor: a long, disruptive defender who sticks even when the shot comes and goes.
Dame Sarr.outlets: SI noted he came into his freshman year as a projected 2026 first-rounder. Sportskeeda cited his 7-foot wingspan.
Dame Sarr.why: His defense is a sure thing. His shooting decides whether he's a first-rounder.

Dash Daniels.off: Secondary ball handler and spot-up shooter.
Dash Daniels.str: He's long and plays hard on defense, against pros. He had 24 and 12 in his opener.
Dash Daniels.weak: He's inconsistent, and 62.1 FT% is a shooting flag.
Dash Daniels.swing: Free-throw percentage, since it tends to predict whether the three is real.
Dash Daniels.why_comp: Dyson, his brother, is the ceiling: a long guard who leads the league in steals. Dosunmu is the 6'5" two-way combo guard. Green is the floor: an Aussie wing defender who stuck in a role.
Dash Daniels.outlets: Matt Babcock said Daniels has a chance to become a very effective two-way player. Consensus has him at 36.0.
Dash Daniels.why: His defense translates. His creation and shooting are still question marks.

Flory Bidunga.str: He has a 40.5" max vertical and a 7'3" wingspan, and he was Big 12 Defensive Player of the Year.
Flory Bidunga.weak: He's undersized for a center who doesn't shoot. He's also older, 22.1 on draft night.
Flory Bidunga.swing: Switching onto guards, since his height means he has to.
Flory Bidunga.why_comp: Capela is the vertical rim runner and rebounder who started for years. Gafford is the bouncy, efficient backup or spot starter. Bona is the floor: an undersized, athletic big who sticks.
Flory Bidunga.outlets: Last Word on Sports named Clint Capela and Adem Bona. NBADraft.net comps him to Chimezie Metu.
Flory Bidunga.why: His athleticism and defensive resume are real. His height caps the ceiling.

Pryce Sandfort.off: Shooting off screens and in handoffs.
Pryce Sandfort.str: He's one of the best shooters in college, with wing size, and he hit 129 threes last year.
Pryce Sandfort.weak: He'll be 23.0 on draft night, and his defense and athleticism are average.
Pryce Sandfort.swing: Whether he can defend well enough to stay on the floor.
Pryce Sandfort.why_comp: Robinson is the movement shooter whose gravity changes an offense. Hauser is the 6'7" shooter who sticks on a good team. Kispert is the floor: a big-wing shooter with a steady role.
Pryce Sandfort.outlets: No Ceilings called his shooting gravity elite. Consensus has him at 48.6.
Pryce Sandfort.why: NBA teams always need shooting, and his is real. His age keeps him in the second-round range.

Matt Able.str: He's a good shooter with guard size, and he tested well at the combine.
Matt Able.weak: He barely rebounds, and his on-ball creation is unproven.
Matt Able.why_comp: Nesmith is the shooter-defender wing who became a starter. Christie is the 6'5" two-way shooting guard. Joe is the floor: a shooting specialist who sticks.
Matt Able.outlets: NBADraft.net's comps are Aaron Nesmith / Quentin Grimes. Per SI, nine of 10 executives polled said he should return to college.
Matt Able.why: His shooting and size get him drafted. He needs more on-ball work to move up.

Austin Goosby.off: Plays both guard spots and pushes in transition.
Austin Goosby.str: His size, athleticism and passing feel stand out. 4.3 assists and 5.0 rebounds is a nice all-around line.
Austin Goosby.weak: 43.1 TS% is very poor, and his scoring hasn't translated yet.
Austin Goosby.why_comp: White is the athletic combo guard whose shot came around, turning him into a 20-point scorer. Mann is the creator-scorer bench guard. Bufkin is the floor: a long combo guard who hangs on while developing.
Austin Goosby.outlets: ESPN has him No. 13. ESPN's Sweeney said he moved the needle with NBA scouts during McDonald's All-American practices.
Austin Goosby.why: I need to see the efficiency before I buy ESPN's ranking.

Maximo Adams.off: Score-first wing with a midrange game.
Maximo Adams.def: Guards bigger wings and crashes the glass.
Maximo Adams.str: 8.4 rebounds is elite for a wing. He has size and versatility.
Maximo Adams.weak: 47.8 TS% and 5-18 from three. His defense is still an adjustment.
Maximo Adams.swing: Turning his midrange game into threes.
Maximo Adams.why_comp: Harris is the big-bodied scoring forward with a smooth midrange game. Ingram is the rebounding, versatile combo forward. Phillips is the floor: a long wing who sticks on defense and athleticism.
Maximo Adams.outlets: Roundtable said his physical profile and versatility bring former Tar Heel Harrison Ingram to mind.
Maximo Adams.why: His rebounding and size are real. His efficiency needs to come up.

Trey McKenney.off: Scoring guard who attacks downhill and shoots off the catch.
Trey McKenney.str: He's built like a pro, he can score in bunches, and his 88.9 FT% backs up the shot.
Trey McKenney.weak: Decision-making. Last year, 24% of his pick-and-roll possessions ended in turnovers.
Trey McKenney.swing: Running pick-and-roll without turning it over.
Trey McKenney.why_comp: Powell is the strong 6'4" scorer who became a 20-point guy. Hardaway is the bench scorer who shoots off movement. Walter is the floor: a strong-bodied shooting guard who sticks as a shooter.
Trey McKenney.outlets: A Busting Brackets writer compared his role to Jrue Holiday on the 2024 Celtics. McKenney said his game resembles Jalen Brunson and Devin Booker.
Trey McKenney.why: He's a real scorer. His playmaking decisions keep him out of the first round for now.

Matas Vokietaitis.str: He scores efficiently through contact. He's averaging 20.7 points on 73.4% shooting.
Matas Vokietaitis.weak: He's an old junior, doesn't shoot from outside, and isn't much of a passer (0.5 assists).
Matas Vokietaitis.why_comp: Edey is the efficient, physical post center who starts. Richards is a big-bodied backup who finishes well. Bradley is the floor: a third center who sticks.
Matas Vokietaitis.outlets: NBADraft.net comps him to Jock Landale / Brian Scalabrine and calls him a physically imposing 7-footer.
Matas Vokietaitis.why: He's productive, but traditional centers go late.

Cameron Williams.off: Face-up four who spaces and runs the floor.
Cameron Williams.str: He's long and mobile, and he blocks 1.6 shots in under 11 minutes.
Cameron Williams.weak: He's only playing 10.8 minutes, and at 210 he's thin.
Cameron Williams.swing: Earning minutes on a deep Duke roster.
Cameron Williams.why_comp: Isaac is the long, switchable defender who can shoot. Boucher is a rangy shot blocker who stretches the floor. Gueye is the floor: a long, mobile forward who hangs on a roster.
Cameron Williams.outlets: NBADraft.net's comps are Evan Mobley / Jabari Smith. Before the season, ESPN's Jeremy Woo had him going 10th.
Cameron Williams.why: His tools are lottery level. In 10.8 minutes a game we haven't seen much yet.

Babatunde Oladotun.off: Big wing who scores on jumpers.
Babatunde Oladotun.str: He's a smooth 6'10" scorer with range, and he's one of the youngest players on the board.
Babatunde Oladotun.weak: He's averaging 4.8 points in 15 minutes, and at 202 he's very thin. He missed most of his senior year with an ankle injury.
Babatunde Oladotun.swing: Strength. Can he hold his spots against college bodies?
Babatunde Oladotun.why_comp: Ingram is the thin, long shot-maker who became a primary scorer. Jovic is the skilled big wing in a rotation role. Knox is the floor: a big wing who keeps getting chances because of his size and shooting.
Babatunde Oladotun.outlets: NBADraft.net's comp is Brandon Ingram. He reclassified from 2027 to 2026.
Babatunde Oladotun.why: His upside is top 10. His production is nowhere near that yet.

Davion Thompson.off: Runs the offense and shoots off the catch.
Davion Thompson.str: 6.5 assists and 44% from three, and he should have been a high school senior this year.
Davion Thompson.weak: He's 6'2" and 180, and teams will test him on defense.
Davion Thompson.why_comp: Conley is the crafty, smart point guard who shoots and runs a team for a decade. Tyus Jones is the steady, low-turnover backup. Tre Jones is the floor: a smart backup point guard who sticks.
Davion Thompson.outlets: SI noted that his length causes disruption on defense despite his size.
Davion Thompson.why: His point guard skills are real right away. His size caps where he goes.

Shelton Henderson.off: Attacks downhill and plays some point forward.
Shelton Henderson.str: He's strong with the ball and finishes through contact, and 8.2 rebounds is great for a wing.
Shelton Henderson.swing: The jumper. Nothing else matters as much.
Shelton Henderson.why_comp: Castle is the strong guard-wing who plays several positions without a jumper. Whitmore is the strong downhill wing who scores in bursts. Terry is the floor: a big wing who sticks on defense and energy.
Shelton Henderson.outlets: A Miami coach compared his usage to Stephon Castle at UConn.
Shelton Henderson.why: His tools and production are first-round level. The shot isn't there yet.

Milan Momcilovic.off: Stretch four who shoots threes and posts up mismatches.
Milan Momcilovic.str: He shot 48.7% from three last year and set Iowa State's record with 136 made threes.
Milan Momcilovic.weak: A 32" max vertical, short arms, and slow feet on defense.
Milan Momcilovic.swing: Finding a matchup he can guard in the NBA.
Milan Momcilovic.why_comp: McDermott is the forward who lasted years on shooting alone. Niang is the 6'7" stretch forward a good team plays. Mykhailiuk is the floor: a shooter who keeps getting contracts.
Milan Momcilovic.outlets: NBADraft.net comps him to Nikola Mirotic / Davis Bertans and lists a 6'9.25" wingspan and 32.0 max vertical.
Milan Momcilovic.why: His shooting gets him drafted. His defense keeps him in round two.

Jordan Scott.def: Rangy help defender who takes tough assignments.
Jordan Scott.str: He blocked 6 shots against No. 2 Duke, and he's hitting 39.1% from three.
Jordan Scott.weak: At 190 he's light, and he doesn't create his own shot.
Jordan Scott.swing: Scoring with the ball in his hands.
Jordan Scott.why_comp: Covington is the rangy 3-and-D forward who racks up blocks and steals. McDaniels is a long role wing. Edwards is the floor: a long 3-and-D wing who sticks.
Jordan Scott.outlets: Spartan Avenue described him as a 6-foot-7 wing who can shoot the three and defend. Consensus has him at 44.0.
Jordan Scott.why: He's the classic 3-and-D archetype, with upside if he adds strength.

Cameron Houindo.str: He's an explosive athlete with strength, and he was MVP at ANGT and Basketball Without Borders.
Cameron Houindo.weak: His minutes are small. He hasn't made a three as a pro, and his free throws are around 61%.
Cameron Houindo.swing: Developing any skill beyond the rim.
Cameron Houindo.why_comp: Clarke is the bouncy, efficient forward who wins with athleticism and touch. Achiuwa is a strong, athletic energy big. Metu is the floor: an athletic big who bounces around the league.
Cameron Houindo.outlets: PIRB Scouting's Pierre Bouthors compared his development path to Clarke's early days.
Cameron Houindo.why: He has the athleticism. He's too raw to rank higher.

Pavle Backo.off: Stretch five who posts up and passes out of the post.
Pavle Backo.str: He's a big body with real touch and range, and he was U19 ABA MVP two years running.
Pavle Backo.weak: He's not a great athlete, and only 4.2 rebounds in 20 minutes is low.
Pavle Backo.why_comp: Vucevic is the skilled lefty stretch big who starts for a decade. Wagner is the lefty, high-energy stretch big in a rotation. Garza is the floor: a skilled post scorer who sticks as a third center.
Pavle Backo.outlets: SI noted that as a lefty he shoots the three with more confidence than Suigo. Consensus has him at 64.7.
Pavle Backo.why: He's productive in a pro league, and his skill as a lefty big is real. His athleticism caps him.

Amare Bynum.off: Rolling and cutting four, with some pick-and-pop.
Amare Bynum.def: Energetic four who protects the rim.
Amare Bynum.str: He's efficient (65.2 TS%) and has been Ohio State's best frontcourt player so far.
Amare Bynum.weak: The three (5-16) isn't consistent yet, and 6'8" is in-between for an NBA four.
Amare Bynum.why_comp: Washington is the strong four who became a starter once the corner three came around. Toppin is the bouncy energy four who scores in transition. Watford is the floor: a versatile forward who keeps a roster spot.
Amare Bynum.outlets: Rivals' Eric Bossi called him a live-bodied, energetic and versatile player.
Amare Bynum.why: He's productive and efficient. His position is the question.

Massamba Diop.off: Roller and short-roll passer, with some pop.
Massamba Diop.str: At 7'1" he moves his feet very well. He blocked 2.1 shots a game last year at Arizona State.
Massamba Diop.weak: He's older (22.5 on draft night), and his production dropped after the transfer.
Massamba Diop.swing: Strength, so he can hold up against NBA centers.
Massamba Diop.why_comp: Claxton is the mobile 7-footer who switches and became a starter. Queta is the big who earned a real role after a slow start. Hayes is the floor: a bouncy backup center.
Massamba Diop.outlets: Ersin Demir wrote that at 7-foot-1 the Senegal-born center has tremendous mobility.
Massamba Diop.why: His mobility makes him a real prospect. His production and age keep him in the second round.

Rueben Chinyelu.str: He had the longest wingspan at the 2026 combine, and he set Florida's records for double-doubles and offensive rebounds.
Rueben Chinyelu.weak: He's 23.7 on draft night, has no jumper, and his numbers are down this year.
Rueben Chinyelu.swing: Showing he can switch and guard in space at the NBA level.
Rueben Chinyelu.why_comp: Okongwu is the undersized, long, switchable starting center. Stewart is the physical enforcer who rebounds and switches. Biyombo is the floor: a length-and-effort big who lasts 15 seasons.
Rueben Chinyelu.outlets: No Ceilings described him as a min-maxed player any NBA team would have a role for. Babcock Hoops called him a rugged, high-motor interior big man.
Rueben Chinyelu.why: His length and physicality are real. His age caps the upside.

Alvaro Folgueiras.str: 47.4% from three plus 3.5 assists. He was Horizon League Player of the Year at Robert Morris.
Alvaro Folgueiras.weak: He's a below-average athlete, and his U20 EuroBasket showing raised quickness questions.
Alvaro Folgueiras.swing: Holding up on defense against NBA fours.
Alvaro Folgueiras.why_comp: Aldama is the Spanish stretch four who passes and earned a big role. Saric is the skilled passing four in a rotation role. Hernangomez is the floor: a stretch four who bounces between rosters.
Alvaro Folgueiras.outlets: Draft Stack suggested he could carve out a role similar to Santi Aldama in the NBA.
Alvaro Folgueiras.why: He has the skill. His athleticism keeps him in the second round.

Cheickh Niang.str: He's an explosive athlete playing pro minutes at 18, and he was All-Star Five at U18 EuroBasket.
Cheickh Niang.weak: He's thin on production and inconsistent as a shooter (22% last year).
Cheickh Niang.swing: Whether the three-point jump is real.
Cheickh Niang.why_comp: Mann is the strong, athletic wing who starts on a good team. Ellis is an athletic defender who also shoots. Clark is the floor: a bouncy wing defender who sticks.
Cheickh Niang.outlets: EuroLeague described him as an integral part of Trento's rotation in his first full pro season. His brother Saliou was a 2025 second-rounder.
Cheickh Niang.why: He's young and athletic, with a real shot. He's still a project.

Christian Collins.str: He has length, motor and versatility. He averaged 26.1 points as a high school senior.
Christian Collins.weak: He's played three games after the foot injury, and at 200 he's thin.
Christian Collins.why_comp: Camara is the wiry, high-motor defender who became an All-Defense-level starter. Vanderbilt is the rangy energy forward who defends and rebounds. Miller is the floor: a long, athletic forward who sticks.
Christian Collins.outlets: NBADraft.net's comp is Jarred Vanderbilt, and it cites his 7'1" wingspan.
Christian Collins.why: He was a top-five recruit, but his injury means we've barely seen him.

Paul McNeil.off: Shooting off movement and the catch.
Paul McNeil.str: He shot 42.7% from three last year and is at 41.8% on volume this year.
Paul McNeil.weak: He hits only 39.7% from the field, and he has little game inside the arc.
Paul McNeil.why_comp: Allen is the 6'4" shooter who became a high-volume role player. Dick is the big shooter who's still finding his role. Hawkins is the floor: a slim, high-volume shooter who sticks.
Paul McNeil.outlets: No Ceilings called him a lights-out marksman with an unorthodox statistical profile.
Paul McNeil.why: His shooting is real. The rest of his game is thin.

Bryson Howard.str: He's a long lefty shooter, and he was Texas Gatorade Player of the Year.
Bryson Howard.weak: He's playing 9.8 minutes, and he's shooting 31.2%.
Bryson Howard.swing: Earning minutes on Duke's deep roster.
Bryson Howard.why_comp: Podziemski is the lefty 6'4" shooter who rebounds and does everything. Braun is the two-way wing who defends, rebounds and hits enough shots to start. Miller is the floor: a wing who sticks on effort.
Bryson Howard.outlets: SI described him as a long and athletic left-handed shooter. Jon Scheyer said he can guard the opposing team's best player.
Bryson Howard.why: His recruiting profile is high. His freshman minutes are low.

Jeremy Fears Jr..off: Runs pick-and-roll and creates for others.
Jeremy Fears Jr..str: He led the country with 9.4 assists last year and is an AP second-team All-American. He had 18 points and 11 assists against No. 2 Duke.
Jeremy Fears Jr..weak: He's 6'2" with a 6'4" wingspan, and he shot only 32.1% from three last year.
Jeremy Fears Jr..why_comp: Nembhard is the smart, tough point guard who starts on a good team. McConnell is the pass-first backup who changes games with pace and pressure. Butler is the floor: a backup point guard who sticks.
Jeremy Fears Jr..outlets: SI said that at 6-foot-2 with a 32% three-point percentage, there are questions about his fit.
Jeremy Fears Jr..why: He's one of the best college point guards. His size and shooting cap his draft range.

Karter Knox.str: He has a 39.5" max vertical and a strong frame, and 8.5 rebounds is strong for a wing.
Karter Knox.weak: He's 3-13 from three and doesn't create much off the dribble.
Karter Knox.why_comp: Martin is the athletic, tough wing who became a playoff contributor. Agbaji is the strong 6'5" wing in a role. Langford is the floor: a strong wing who hangs on.
Karter Knox.outlets: NBADraft.net's comp is Romeo Langford. It lists a 6'10.25" wingspan and 39.5 max vertical.
Karter Knox.why: He has the athleticism. The shot isn't there.

Stefan Vaaks.off: Shoots off movement and runs some pick-and-roll.
Stefan Vaaks.str: He has size and shot-making, plus real creation. He took 250+ threes at Providence last year.
Stefan Vaaks.weak: He's shooting 32.7% from three, and he'll be 22.1 on draft night.
Stefan Vaaks.swing: The three. If it's at 37% by March, he's a draft pick.
Stefan Vaaks.why_comp: Bogdanovic is the big Euro shooter-creator who scores in bunches. Fontecchio is the 6'7" Euro shooting wing in a rotation role. Satoransky is the floor: a big Euro guard who stays because he can handle and pass.
Stefan Vaaks.outlets: Jonathan Wasserman noted Estonia World Cup qualifier games where he combined for 39 points on 15-31 with 12 assists. Ersin Demir called him a solidly built guard in a wing's body.
Stefan Vaaks.why: His size and skill fit the NBA. His shot hasn't been consistent enough yet.

Johann Grünloh.str: 3.0 blocks a game, and he passes well for a center. He played pro ball in the German BBL.
Johann Grünloh.weak: He's 2-16 from three, and he was billed as a floor-spacer.
Johann Grünloh.swing: The three. It decides whether he's a rotation big or a third center.
Johann Grünloh.why_comp: Kessler is the 7-foot shot blocker who anchors a defense. Eubanks is the dependable backup center. Bryant is the floor: a big who stays on the roster and flashes some range.
Johann Grünloh.outlets: NBADraft.net's comp is Tiago Splitter / Jakob Poeltl. SI noted his ability as a floor spacer and passer from the center position.
Johann Grünloh.why: His rim protection is real. His shot hasn't been there.

Moustapha Thiam.def: Rim protector who can play outside drop coverage.
Moustapha Thiam.str: His length and mobility, plus 2.8 blocks in 23 minutes.
Moustapha Thiam.weak: 40% from the field and 48.8 TS% is poor for a center. He's light.
Moustapha Thiam.swing: Finishing. He shot 68.9% at the rim last year.
Moustapha Thiam.why_comp: Robinson is the long shot blocker who anchors a playoff defense. Bol is the 7-footer with length and range who sticks on a roster. Jackson is the floor: a bouncy, long backup.
Moustapha Thiam.outlets: NBADraft.net's comp is Mo Bamba. No Ceilings mapped out a path for him to join Wolf and Mara as Michigan big men taken in the first round.
Moustapha Thiam.why: His tools are real, and his production has been inconsistent.

Arafan Diane.str: He has a huge body plus footwork, touch and passing. He was the No. 1 center in the 2026 class.
Arafan Diane.weak: He's only playing 12.3 minutes and getting just 1.8 rebounds. His mobility in space is a question.
Arafan Diane.swing: Conditioning and mobility. He needs to play real minutes.
Arafan Diane.why_comp: Freedom is the big post scorer and rebounder who started for years. Okafor is the skilled post center who stuck as a backup. Jemison is the floor: a big body who hangs on as a third center.
Arafan Diane.outlets: Sportskeeda reported his coaches call him the "African Jokic" for his footwork and touch. Hakeem Olajuwon praised him to PaperCity after watching him at a camp. Consensus has him at 15.0.
Arafan Diane.why: He has the size and skill. In 12 minutes a night we haven't seen enough.

Klark Reithauser.off: Big wing who shoots and runs some offense.
Klark Reithauser.def: Active wing who gets into passing lanes.
Klark Reithauser.str: He shot 37.4% on volume at 6'8", and he made the NextGen EuroLeague All-Star Five.
Klark Reithauser.weak: He's injured, with no pro production this year. January is the earliest likely return.
Klark Reithauser.swing: Getting healthy and playing pro minutes before the deadline to declare.
Klark Reithauser.why_comp: Bogdanovic is the 6'8" shooter who scores off movement and became a starter. Osman is the 6'7" Euro wing who shoots and handles in a role. Nwora is the floor: a big shooting wing who hangs on.
Klark Reithauser.outlets: No outlet comps. These are my picks, based on his archetype.
Klark Reithauser.why: His production in the youth leagues is first-round level. The injury is why he's not higher.

Jaxon Richardson.str: His explosiveness is real, and so are the blocks and rebounding for a wing.
Jaxon Richardson.weak: He shot 16% from three and 54% on free throws on the 2025 EYBL circuit.
Jaxon Richardson.swing: The jumper. Nothing else matters as much.
Jaxon Richardson.why_comp: Bridges is the explosive wing-forward who grew into a scorer. Watson is the athletic wing who blocks shots in a role. Culver is the floor: an athletic wing who keeps getting chances.
Jaxon Richardson.outlets: ESPN's Paul Biancardi compared him to his father, Jason Richardson.
Jaxon Richardson.why: He has the athleticism. The shot is far away.

Juke Harris.str: He scored 21.4 a game last year at Wake Forest. He has size and length.
Juke Harris.weak: 31.1% from the field and 42.4 TS% at Tennessee. The transfer hasn't worked so far.
Juke Harris.why_comp: Hood is the long, smooth scorer who was a starter. Ross is the lanky bench scorer who heats up. Juzang is the floor: a scorer who sticks on a two-way deal.
Juke Harris.outlets: FanVerdicts compared him to DeMar DeRozan (lite). Babcock Hoops called him a long, skilled perimeter scorer.
Juke Harris.why: Last year was real. This year has been bad.

Deron Rippey Jr..off: Lead guard who attacks off the bounce.
Deron Rippey Jr..str: He's explosive and defends hard. He was a McDonald's All-American and Hoop Summit pick.
Deron Rippey Jr..weak: He's averaging 2.8 points on 30% shooting, and he's small.
Deron Rippey Jr..why_comp: Ivey is the explosive downhill guard with real scoring. Anthony is the bench scorer and creator. Smith is the floor: a small guard who scores and hangs on.
Deron Rippey Jr..outlets: SI said he shows "shades of Ja Morant." Rivals said NBA scouts liked his defense on the ball.
Deron Rippey Jr..why: His recruiting profile is lottery level. His production isn't there yet.

David Mirkovic.off: Point forward who also spaces the floor.
David Mirkovic.str: His skill at his size. He averaged 13 and 8 on a Final Four team last year.
David Mirkovic.weak: He's injured, and his athleticism and lateral quickness are questions.
David Mirkovic.swing: Coming back and playing at last year's level.
David Mirkovic.why_comp: Randle is the strong four who handles, shoots and rebounds. Anderson is the crafty point forward in a role. Hezonja is the floor: a skilled Euro forward who had an NBA run.
David Mirkovic.outlets: Illinois on SI said he has a very particular set of skills. CBS has him highest, at No. 11.
David Mirkovic.why: I'm ranking him on last year's production, and lower because of the injuries.

Cayden Boozer.str: He's a strong, smart passer. CBS calls him the best pure facilitator on Duke.
Cayden Boozer.weak: He doesn't score much, and his shooting is a small sample.
Cayden Boozer.swing: Scoring enough to keep defenses honest.
Cayden Boozer.why_comp: Smart is the strong, tough guard who defends and makes winning plays. Joseph is the steady backup point guard. Forrest is the floor: a strong backup guard who sticks on defense.
Cayden Boozer.outlets: On3 called him a strong-framed and aggressive point guard.
Cayden Boozer.why: He's a smart role player. His scoring keeps him low.

JT Toppin.def: Active four who protects the rim.
JT Toppin.str: His production is elite. He was Big 12 Player of the Year in 2025 and averaged 21.8 and 10.8 last year.
JT Toppin.weak: He has no jumper, and he's coming back from an ACL tear. He'll be 22 on draft night.
JT Toppin.swing: Getting back to his old explosiveness after the ACL.
JT Toppin.why_comp: Collins is the athletic, productive scoring four. Jackson-Davis is the athletic interior big who rolls, finishes and blocks shots. Tshiebwe is the floor: a college star rebounder who hangs on.
JT Toppin.outlets: NBADraft.net's comp is Larry Nance Jr. Draft Stack compared him to Jarred Vanderbilt.
JT Toppin.why: His production is first-round level. The injury, his age and the missing jumper put him here.

Brandon McCoy.str: He was a top-10 recruit, with elite athleticism and defensive tools.
Brandon McCoy.weak: He won't play a college game before the draft, and his jumper was a question even before the injury.
Brandon McCoy.swing: Whether he enters the 2027 draft at all.
Brandon McCoy.why_comp: Green is the explosive 6'4" scorer who gets to the rim. Wallace is the defensive combo guard who hits enough shots to start. Brown is the floor: a versatile guard-wing who sticks.
Brandon McCoy.outlets: NBADraft.net's comp is Troy Brown. SI called him a top-10 candidate before the injury. Consensus has him at 16.4.
Brandon McCoy.why: His talent is lottery level. He'll have no college tape and a recent ACL tear, so he's on the watchlist.

Adam Atamna.str: He scores, and he's playing pro minutes at 18. He won U18 EuroBasket silver with France.
Adam Atamna.weak: His pro production is modest, and he's still finding a role in Ulm's rotation.
Adam Atamna.swing: Earning real BBL or EuroCup minutes.
Adam Atamna.why_comp: Poole is the scoring combo guard who can take over a game. Jerome is the crafty combo guard who carved out a role. Ntilikina is the floor: a French guard who stuck five years on his defense.
Adam Atamna.outlets: Esquire Middle East reported that he studies Luka Doncic and Devin Booker. B/R ranked him the No. 49 international guard in September.
Adam Atamna.why: He's young, with a pro resume. He's here as a watchlist name.

Killyan Toure.def: Guards the other team's best guard.
Killyan Toure.str: His defense on the ball is elite. Babcock Hoops calls him one of the premier on-ball defenders in college basketball.
Killyan Toure.weak: His offense is limited, and he's had shoulder surgery.
Killyan Toure.why_comp: Shumpert is the strong, physical defensive guard who started on a title team. Carter is the point-of-attack pest in a rotation role. Springer is the floor: a defensive guard who hangs on.
Killyan Toure.outlets: NBADraft.net's comps are Gary Payton II / Iman Shumpert.
Killyan Toure.why: His defense gets him drafted. He'll have half a season to show his offense.

John Blackwell.off: Scoring guard off movement and pull-ups.
John Blackwell.str: He averaged 19.1 points and shot 38.9% from three last year at Wisconsin.
John Blackwell.weak: He's shooting 29.8% and doesn't pass much at Duke. He also measured a wingspan shorter than his height.
John Blackwell.swing: Getting back to his Wisconsin efficiency.
John Blackwell.why_comp: Clarkson is the 6'4" bench scorer who won Sixth Man of the Year. Strus is the shooter who earned a real role. Edwards is the floor: an undersized scorer who got a look.
John Blackwell.outlets: Jim Sumner noted it is very unusual for a player to have a shorter wingspan than his height. SI lists him as a projected second-round pick.
John Blackwell.why: His scoring track record is real. His start at Duke is a red flag.

Neoklis Avdalas.str: He's a 6'8" passer and handler with real feel. He had 4.6 assists at Virginia Tech.
Neoklis Avdalas.weak: He shot 31.4% from three last year and is 2-10 now. Defense and strength are concerns.
Neoklis Avdalas.why_comp: Turkoglu is the 6'10" point forward who ran an offense. Banton is the big guard who handles in a backup role. Sirvydis is the floor: a Euro wing who had a short NBA run.
Neoklis Avdalas.outlets: NBADraft.net's comp is Deni Avdija. Sportscasting compared him to Hedo Turkoglu and Kyle Anderson.
Neoklis Avdalas.why: His playmaking at his size is rare. His shooting and defense keep him low.

Joseph Tugler.def: Switches everything and protects the rim.
Joseph Tugler.str: He's an elite defender. Houston had an 89.3 defensive rating with him on the floor, the best in the country.
Joseph Tugler.weak: He has no jumper, and his scoring is limited.
Joseph Tugler.why_comp: Tillman is the undersized, smart defensive big who won a title. Reed is a high-energy forward who gets steals and blocks. Bell is the floor: a switchable defender who played a few NBA seasons.
Joseph Tugler.outlets: A 2025 Yahoo scouting report credited his 7-foot-6 wingspan and defensive versatility.
Joseph Tugler.why: His defense is first-round level. His offense is second-round level at best.

Roman Domon.str: He's a 6'9" creator who averages 23 points and gets to the line (11.6 attempts a game).
Roman Domon.weak: He's 7-41 from three, and he shot 36.8% from three last year.
Roman Domon.swing: Whether the three-point shot comes back.
Roman Domon.why_comp: Fournier is the French scorer who averaged 17 to 19 points as a starter. Luwawu-Cabarrot is the French wing who had a real NBA run. Rupert is the floor: a long French wing who sticks on a roster.
Roman Domon.outlets: SI described him as a 6-foot-9 forward with ball skills. He won the 2026 MVC Sixth Man of the Year as a freshman.
Roman Domon.why: He's productive with real skill. His shooting has to come back.

Miles Byrd.str: 4.3 steals and 1.5 blocks a game. His defensive playmaking is rare.
Miles Byrd.weak: He's shooting 22.7% from three and 34.4% from the field. He's thin.
Miles Byrd.why_comp: Caruso is the defensive playmaker who wins on steals and smart plays. Payton is an athletic defender with steals and blocks in a role. Anderson is the floor: a long wing who gets looks.
Miles Byrd.outlets: NBADraft.net's comp is RJ Hunter. SI cited a Ringer note that he's one of 13 players since 2007-08 with steal and block rates over 4%.
Miles Byrd.why: His defensive profile is rare. His shooting has gone backward.

Jacob Cofie.off: Rolling four who also handles a bit.
Jacob Cofie.str: He's an elite athlete for his size, and he got a call-up from the G League Combine to the NBA Combine.
Jacob Cofie.weak: His production is down, and his jumper (1-8) is unproven.
Jacob Cofie.why_comp: Nance is the athletic, smart big who passes and defends. Nnaji is the athletic backup big. Garuba is the floor: a defensive big who hangs on.
Jacob Cofie.outlets: Eric Musselman called him extremely versatile with elite athleticism. No Ceilings asked whether he can emerge as a first-round pick.
Jacob Cofie.why: He has the athleticism. His production has gone backward.

Nik Khamenia.off: Connective forward who spaces the floor.
Nik Khamenia.str: He's a high-feel passer, and he's 6-11 from three so far.
Nik Khamenia.weak: Only three games so far. He had a rough freshman year at Duke (5.7 ppg).
Nik Khamenia.swing: Keeping the shooting going over a full season.
Nik Khamenia.why_comp: Prince is the 6'7" shooting forward who started and lasted. Highsmith is the 3-and-D forward in a rotation role. Champagnie is the floor: a shooting forward who sticks.
Nik Khamenia.outlets: Rivals' Jamie Shaw called him a quick processor with excellent passing touch.
Nik Khamenia.why: It's a small sample, but a good one.

Cole Cloer.str: He was a top-30 recruit with a reputation as a great shooter.
Cole Cloer.weak: He's 5-27 from three, which is the opposite of his reputation.
Cole Cloer.why_comp: Moody is the long 3-and-D wing who grew into a rotation role. Knecht is a scorer-shooter in a role. Howard is the floor: a big shooting wing who hangs on.
Cole Cloer.outlets: Labaron Philon said it was crazy how he shoots the ball.
Cole Cloer.why: I'm betting on the shooting reputation. The results haven't shown it yet.

Nolan Winter.off: Stretch big who scores from midrange.
Nolan Winter.str: He shot 69% on twos over his career and is the best rebounder in the Big Ten.
Nolan Winter.weak: He's 2-13 from three, 6-16 at the line, and 44.4% from the field. That's a cold start.
Nolan Winter.why_comp: Kaminsky is the skilled 7-foot Wisconsin big who had a long career. Leuer is the skilled four or five who stuck. Potter is the floor: a stretch big who gets two-way deals.
Nolan Winter.outlets: The Star Tribune reported Wisconsin's coaches compared him to Jon Leuer. Ersin Demir called him the best rebounder in the Big Ten.
Nolan Winter.why: He's skilled and efficient, but his start has been rough.

Nigel James.off: Lead guard who gets downhill and creates.
Nigel James.str: He's strong and athletic, and he was Big East Freshman of the Year with a 38-point game last year.
Nigel James.weak: 32.1% from the field and 2-17 from three is a very cold start.
Nigel James.why_comp: Nunn is the strong scoring guard who made the All-Rookie team. Pippen is the small playmaker who stuck. Howard is the floor: a small scoring guard who got a look.
Nigel James.outlets: He told Prospective Insight that he watches Donovan Mitchell a lot.
Nigel James.why: Last year's production gets him on the board, but his start has been bad.
